9.1|In the context of organizational communication channels, which of the following best represents the medium through which a message travels?|The mental translation of symbols into ideas|The physical or virtual pathway used to transmit the message from sender to receiver|The final evaluation score of an employee's output|The hierarchical level where policy decisions are enacted|Option B|The channel or message medium is the pathway—such as email, face-to-face conversation, or memos—used to carry the message between sender and receiver.

11.1|Which of the following performance appraisal techniques explicitly focuses on documenting specific behaviors that distinguish outstanding job performance from subpar execution?|Graphic Rating Scales|Critical Incident Method|Management by Objectives|Forced Distribution Ranking|Option C|The critical incident method relies on supervisors logging specific, concrete examples of exceptionally good or poor worker behaviors rather than vague traits.|
11.1|What defines a modern performance appraisal technique that emphasizes collaborative goal-setting and measurable outcomes between managers and employees?|360-Degree Feedback|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales|Management by Objectives|Paired Comparison Ranking|Option C|Management by Objectives is a modern approach where managers and subordinates jointly set objectives, aligning individual targets with broader organizational goals.|
11.1|When a supervisor allows a single outstanding trait of an employee to positively influence all other evaluated performance dimensions, which rating bias is occurring?|Horns Effect|Leniency Bias|Central Tendency Bias|Halo Effect|Option D|The halo effect occurs when a rater's generalized positive impression on one dimension spills over to unjustly inflate evaluations across all other performance categories.|
11.1|Which appraisal error describes a rater's tendency to consistently evaluate nearly all subordinates as average, avoiding the use of extremely high or low ratings?|Strictness Bias|Central Tendency Bias|Recency Effect|Halo Effect|Option B|Central tendency bias happens when managers cluster all ratings in the middle of the scale to avoid confrontation or having to justify extreme scores.|
11.1|What is the core characteristic that distinguishes traditional performance appraisal rating scales from modern techniques like BARS?|Traditional scales measure personality traits and behaviors using numerical values without specific behavioral anchors|Traditional techniques require multi-source feedback from peers and subordinates simultaneously|Traditional methods rely exclusively on self-assessments conducted without supervisory oversight|Traditional systems evaluate organizational profitability instead of individual output|Option A|Traditional rating scales often use abstract traits and numeric scores without detailed behavioral descriptions, whereas BARS uses concrete behavioral anchors.|
11.1|Which modern appraisal technique incorporates performance evaluations from supervisors peers subordinates and customers to provide a comprehensive developmental view?|Critical Incident Method|Graphic Rating Scales|360-Degree Feedback|Simple Ranking Technique|Option C|The 360-degree feedback method gathers performance data from multiple stakeholder groups surrounding the employee to offer a well-rounded and comprehensive review.|
11.1|Which rating error occurs when an evaluator permits a single negative characteristic of an employee to disproportionately lower scores across all unrelated performance areas?|Leniency Bias|Horns Effect|Recency Effect|Central Tendency Bias|Option B|The horns effect is the inverse of the halo effect where one perceived negative attribute taints the evaluator's judgment on all other completely unrelated dimensions.|
11.1|How does the recency effect negatively impact the accuracy of a performance appraisal review?|It causes the rater to judge the employee based exclusively on events that occurred during the final weeks of the evaluation period|It forces the rater to compare employees directly against each other rather than against established job standards|It leads the manager to give overly generous ratings to prevent hurt feelings among low-performing staff|It restricts the rating scale to the middle categories, ignoring exceptional performance extremes|Option A|The recency effect occurs when evaluators disproportionately anchor their annual ratings on recent performance events while ignoring earlier performance during the cycle.|
11.1|What is the primary operational weakness of utilizing strictness bias during performance evaluations?|It inflates organizational payroll by forcing unnecessary salary promotions across departments|It systematically lowers performance ratings, demoralizing competent employees and distorting performance metrics|It completely eliminates the need for objective documentation during disciplinary termination procedures|It requires excessive administrative overhead from multi-departmental committees|Option B|Strictness bias involves a rater who is overly harsh, systematically depressing ratings and failing to accurately recognize valid employee contributions.|
11.1|Which appraisal technique combines elements of the critical incident method and graphic rating scales by utilizing measurable behavioral milestones along a numerical continuum?|Paired Comparison|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales|Forced Distribution|Simple Ranking|Option B|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales combine narrative critical incidents with a quantified scale to give raters specific behavioral benchmarks for evaluation.|

12.1|Why is the cost of living considered an important pay determinant for organizations?|It measures the internal productivity and output speed of individual workers|It tracks changes in consumer prices to help employees maintain their purchasing power|It evaluates the relative educational requirements needed for specific administrative tasks|It determines the exact legal tax bracket for corporate payroll deductions|Option B|Cost of living adjustments reflect changes in the prices of consumer goods and services, helping ensure wages retain real purchasing power over time.

14.1|What is the official designation of the administrative body responsible for issuing an initial arbitration award when conciliation fails?|The National Industrial Court of Nigeria|The Industrial Arbitration Panel|The Federal Ministry of Public Service Review Commission|The National Labour Advisory Council|Option B|The Industrial Arbitration Panel (IAP) is the designated statutory body that hears unsettled disputes and hands down an IAP award.
14.1|Which judicial institution possesses exclusive original jurisdiction over trade disputes and labor matters in Nigeria as per the statutory framework?|The Supreme Court of Nigeria|The Federal High Court|The National Industrial Court of Nigeria|The Court of Appeal|Option C|The National Industrial Court of Nigeria (NICN) is vested with exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate industrial relations matters and trade disputes.

14.1|If an internal grievance procedure fails to resolve a dispute, what is typically the immediate next external statutory step?|Mediation involving a voluntary third party within seven days|Direct appeal to the Supreme Court for constitutional interpretation|Immediate liquidation of the corporate entity by the registrar of companies|Mandatory criminal prosecution of the human resources manager|Option A|Following the exhaustion of internal procedures, the framework moves to voluntary mediation, which is expected to occur within seven days.
14.1|Why is the internal grievance procedure prioritized as the foundation of the statutory settlement machinery?|It ensures that all disputes bypass management and go straight to court|It allows organizations to resolve issues swiftly and amicably at the lowest possible level before external escalation|It eliminates the need for trade unions to exist in any modern workplace environment|It guarantees that employees will never receive pay raises or promotions|Option B|An effective internal grievance procedure resolves conflicts early, fostering better employee relations and preventing unnecessary external litigation.
14.1|What distinguishes the Industrial Arbitration Panel from the National Industrial Court of Nigeria in the dispute resolution hierarchy?|The IAP issues preliminary arbitration awards, whereas the NICN possesses exclusive judicial jurisdiction over labor matters|The IAP is a private consulting firm while the NICN is a trade union committee|The NICN handles mediation while the IAP deals exclusively with internal office memos|The IAP has higher legal authority than the NICN in all constitutional matters|Option A|The Industrial Arbitration Panel issues arbitral awards, while the National Industrial Court of Nigeria serves as the specialized court with exclusive judicial jurisdiction.
3.1|Which personnel management approach views the organization as an open system that must continuously adapt to its dynamic external environment?|The Paternalistic Approach|The Human Relations Approach|The Contingency and Social System Approach|The Scientific Management Approach|Option C|The contingency or social system approach views organizations as open systems that survive by successfully adapting to changes in their dynamic external environments.
3.1|In the paternalistic approach to personnel management, what is the primary expectation demanded from employees in exchange for organizational welfare provisions?|High levels of innovation|Total obedience and loyalty|Democratic participation in decision making|Strict adherence to formal bureaucratic rules|Option B|The paternalistic approach relies on management acting as a benevolent father figure that provides employee welfare in exchange for total obedience and loyalty.
3.1|Which key historical development or study heavily influenced the emergence of the human relations approach to personnel management?|The Hawthorne Studies by Elton Mayo|The time and motion studies by Frederick Taylor|The bureaucratic theories by Max Weber|The administrative principles by Henri Fayol|Option A|Elton Mayo and his colleagues conducted the famous Hawthorne Studies, which fundamentally shifted focus toward social and psychological needs in the workplace.
3.1|What core workplace dimension is primarily emphasized by the human relations approach rather than purely economic incentives?|Physical endurance and machine speed|Social and psychological needs of workers|Hierarchical control and command chains|Rigid task specialization and division of labor|Option B|The human relations approach prioritizes social needs group dynamics and psychological factors over viewing employees as mere economic commodities.
3.1|A manager implements regular team-building sessions and open communication channels to improve group dynamics. Which personnel approach is being applied?|The Paternalistic Approach|The Scientific Management Approach|The Human Relations Approach|The Classical Administrative Approach|Option C|Focusing on communication group dynamics and social interactions is a direct application of the human relations approach derived from Hawthorne insights.
3.1|Why is the contingency approach sometimes referred to as the social system approach in personnel management?|It emphasizes treating workers strictly as social family units|It views the organization as a complex set of interdependent human and environmental variables|It relies exclusively on government social welfare programs for funding|It eliminates formal hierarchies in favor of socialist structures|Option B|It is termed a social system approach because it treats organizations as interconnected systems where internal human elements and external environmental factors dynamically interact.
3.1|What is a major limitation or criticism of the paternalistic approach to personnel management?|It promotes excessive employee unionization and strikes|It can stifle employee independence and treat workers as dependent children|It focuses too heavily on mathematical optimization of tasks|It completely ignores employee welfare and safety|Option B|By treating workers like children who need benevolent protection paternalism often stifles autonomy independence and democratic engagement.
3.1|How does the contingency approach differ from rigid traditional models of personnel management?|It prescribes a single universal best way to manage people|It adapts management practices based on specific internal and external situational variables|It rejects all forms of organizational structure|It focuses solely on individual psychological traits without context|Option B|The core premise of the contingency approach is that there is no single best way to manage and practices must adapt to fit specific situational contexts.
3.1|Which approach to personnel management is most closely characterized by management acting as a provider of welfare benefits while retaining strict patriarchal control?|The Human Relations Approach|The Contingency Approach|The Paternalistic Approach|The Systems Approach|Option C|The defining characteristic of the paternalistic approach is management acting as a father figure who provides welfare and care while demanding complete submission and control.
3.1|When a personnel manager analyzes how informal work groups influence productivity and employee morale, which theoretical framework is primarily being utilized?|The Human Relations Approach|The Paternalistic Approach|The Contingency Open-Market Approach|The Classical Bureaucratic Approach|Option A|Informal groups and their impact on morale and productivity are central pillars of the human relations approach established by the Hawthorne Studies.

6.1|Which of the following best defines manpower planning in the context of personnel management?|The systematic process of ensuring the right number and kinds of people are at the right place and time|The daily administrative scheduling of employee shifts and attendance logs|The reactive hiring of candidates only after critical organizational positions become vacant|The process of determining individual employee salary tiers and compensation packages|Option A|Manpower planning is a systematic mechanism designed to align personnel availability with organizational requirements across time and location.
6.1|What is considered the foundational first stage in the manpower planning process?|Analyzing corporate objectives|Conducting external labor market research|Performing internal skills inventories|Reconciling workforce deficits and surpluses|Option A|Manpower planning begins by analyzing corporate objectives to ensure that future personnel strategies directly align with overarching organizational goals.
6.1|During which stage of manpower planning are techniques like trend analysis and ratio analysis typically applied?|Demand forecasting|Supply forecasting|Corporate objective analysis|Deficit and surplus reconciliation|Option A|Demand forecasting utilizes analytical tools such as trend and ratio analysis to project future personnel needs based on business metrics.
6.1|When an organization evaluates its internal skills inventory to understand current workforce capabilities, which stage of the planning process is it executing?|Supply forecasting|Demand forecasting|Corporate objective analysis|Deficit reconciliation|Option A|Supply forecasting involves reviewing internal resources through skills inventories alongside the external market to evaluate existing talent pools.
6.1|What is the primary purpose of the final stage in the four-stage manpower planning process?|Reconciling deficits and surpluses|Establishing initial corporate goals|Forecasting future economic trends|Designing employee compensation structures|Option A|The final stage focuses on reconciling identified workforce deficits or surpluses to bridge the gap between supply and demand.
6.1|If an organization experiences a shortage of skilled personnel during the reconciliation phase, what is the most appropriate strategic response?|Formulating recruitment or training initiatives to cover the gap|Reducing overall business production targets immediately|Ignoring the deficit until natural attrition occurs|Transferring all management responsibilities to external contractors|Option A|A workforce deficit requires proactive interventions such as targeted recruitment, selection, and training to bridge the staffing shortfall.
6.1|Which analytical technique is commonly associated with predicting workforce demand based on historical data patterns?|Trend analysis|Skills inventory mapping|Succession planning auditing|Job evaluation scaling|Option A|Trend analysis evaluates historical business data and staffing patterns to help forecast future personnel demand.
6.1|Why must supply forecasting incorporate both internal skills inventories and external labor market analysis?|To provide a comprehensive view of available talent sources within and outside the firm|To eliminate the need for corporate objective analysis entirely|To ensure that employee salaries remain uniformly low across all industries|To bypass the requirement of reconciling workforce surpluses|Option A|Effective supply forecasting requires examining both internal talent assets and external market conditions to gain a complete picture of available labor.
6.1|In manpower planning, what consequence typically follows a failure to properly execute the demand forecasting stage?|Misalignment between organizational labor requirements and actual staffing levels|Excessive administrative compliance with federal labor laws|Immediate improvement in departmental budget efficiency|Enhanced clarity regarding individual employee job descriptions|Option A|Failing to forecast demand accurately leads to severe misalignments, resulting in costly staffing surpluses or disruptive talent shortages.
6.1|How does manpower planning directly support overall corporate strategy?|By systematically bridging organizational goals with targeted human resource capabilities|By automating the daily payroll distribution process for all staff members|By standardizing disciplinary procedures across different departments|By replacing the need for long-term financial budgeting|Option A|Manpower planning systematically links broader corporate goals with human resource strategies, ensuring the organization has capable personnel to execute its mission.
4.1|What is the fundamental organizational purpose of establishing a formal personnel policy within an enterprise?|To provide standing written principles that guide managerial decisions and eliminate workplace favouritism|To mandate daily tactical task assignments for junior operational supervisors|To dictate specific short term financial compensation packages for executive boards|To replace traditional labor union negotiations with mandatory binding corporate decrees|Option A|Personnel policies act as standing written principles designed to ensure operational consistency and eliminate favouritism across management decisions.
4.1|Which of the following sequences represents the correct chronological stages of personnel policy formulation?|Need identification followed by fact gathering consultation drafting and board approval|Drafting followed by board approval need identification and public consultation|Fact gathering followed immediately by board ratification and final policy drafting|Consultation followed by board approval and subsequent organizational need identification|Option A|The logical formulation sequence begins with recognizing a need and moves through fact gathering consultation drafting and final board approval.
4.1|During the policy formulation process what is the primary objective of the fact gathering stage?|To collect relevant data and contextual insights to ensure the proposed policy is evidence based|To secure immediate final legal authorization from external regulatory authorities|To eliminate all employee feedback mechanisms prior to senior leadership review|To determine exact individual performance bonuses for department heads|Option A|Fact gathering ensures that the subsequent policy is built upon accurate data and a thorough understanding of workplace realities.
4.1|Why is consultation considered a crucial step before drafting a new personnel policy?|It fosters stakeholder buy in and surfaces operational blind spots or potential conflicts|It completely transfers legislative power from the executive board to general staff|It guarantees that every employee receives a promotion upon policy implementation|It replaces the need for formal board approval by securing immediate majority consensus|Option A|Consultation engages stakeholders early to gather diverse perspectives minimize resistance and identify operational issues.
4.1|In the context of workplace ethical codes which principle specifically addresses the prohibition of unwanted physical or verbal advances?|Anti harassment|Anti bribery|Conflict of interest|Confidentiality|Option A|Anti harassment policies explicitly prohibit unwelcome conduct that creates an intimidating or hostile work environment.
4.1|An employee who accepts financial gifts from a supplier in exchange for awarding a lucrative corporate contract is violating which ethical code element?|Anti bribery|Anti harassment|Confidentiality|Need identification|Option A|Accepting unauthorized financial gifts or inducements constitutes a direct violation of anti bribery codes.
4.1|Which ethical standard is breached when an administrative manager awards a major departmental project to their close personal relative without disclosure?|Conflict of interest|Anti harassment|Confidentiality|Fact gathering|Option A|A conflict of interest arises when personal relationships or private interests improperly influence professional duties.
4.1|What is the core function of confidentiality within an organizational ethical code?|To protect sensitive proprietary business information and private employee records from unauthorized disclosure|To ensure that all internal operational meetings are broadcast publicly without restriction|To prevent managers from communicating performance feedback directly to their subordinates|To mandate the complete public disclosure of executive compensation packages|Option A|Confidentiality safeguards critical proprietary data and personal employee records from being leaked or misused.
4.1|How do documented personnel policies directly affect managerial discretion?|They provide a structured boundary that promotes consistency while reducing arbitrary decision making|They completely strip managers of all supervisory authority over daily operations|They eliminate the need for any human resource department oversight|They legally mandate identical salaries for every employee regardless of job role|Option A|Standing policies guide managers to make fair and consistent decisions rather than relying on arbitrary or biased choices.
4.1|What is the final administrative milestone required to officially enact a newly formulated personnel policy?|Board approval|Initial need identification|Informal peer consultation|Preliminary fact gathering|Option A|Board approval gives the drafted policy official institutional legitimacy and binding authority within the enterprise.
8.1|What is the primary operational objective of the recruitment phase in personnel management?|To rigorously evaluate and test applicant qualifications through structured interviews|To attract a sufficiently large and qualified pool of job applicants for open positions|To officially assign the chosen candidate to a specific organizational position|To integrate the newly hired employee into the organizational culture and reduce anxiety|Option B|Recruitment focuses specifically on sourcing and attracting a robust pool of potential candidates from which to select, distinguishing it from selection and placement.

8.1|In the context of the standard selection hurdles sequence, which step typically follows initial application shortlisting?|Conducting comprehensive medical examinations and physical fitness tests|Administering formal employment tests such as aptitude or work sample assessments|Issuing the official binding employment contract and job offer letter|Performing thorough background and professional reference checks|Option B|Employment tests, including aptitude and work sample evaluations, generally follow initial candidate shortlisting before formal interviews and background checks take place.
8.1|What is the fundamental organizational purpose of introducing a structured placement process?|To legally verify an applicant's medical fitness and background credentials|To assign the selected candidate to a specific position suited to their competencies|To reduce early organizational turnover through intensive social events|To advertise open job opportunities to prospective internal and external candidates|Option B|Placement is the strategic administrative act of officially assigning a chosen candidate to a specific job role where their skills match organizational needs.
8.1|What is a primary psychological and administrative goal of conducting a formal induction program?|To test the applicant's raw cognitive aptitude and technical work proficiency|To lower newcomer anxiety and accelerate integration to reduce early turnover|To negotiate starting salary figures and fringe benefit packages with the candidate|To screen out unqualified candidates before the final job offer is extended|Option B|Induction is designed to orient new employees, ease their transition, diminish anxiety, and ultimately minimize premature employee turnover.
8.1|Which selection hurdle involves evaluating a candidate by observing them perform actual tasks related to the prospective job?|Medical and physical fitness examination hurdle|Reference and background verification hurdle|Work sample employment testing hurdle|Initial application shortlisting hurdle|Option C|Work sample tests directly measure a candidate's ability to perform specific tasks required by the job, serving as a practical predictor of future performance.
8.1|What is a distinct advantage of utilizing external recruitment sources compared to internal methods?|It entirely eliminates the financial costs associated with advertising vacancies|It infuses the organization with fresh ideas, new perspectives, and diverse skill sets|It guarantees immediate familiarity with internal company policies and workflows|It bypasses the need for employment testing and background reference checks|Option B|External recruitment brings in fresh talent with new viewpoints and experiences, helping to prevent organizational stagnation and expand the skill base.
8.1|During which stage of the selection process are previous employers and character references typically contacted?|Prior to the initial shortlisting of candidate resumes and application forms|Immediately after advertising the vacancy to the external labor market|As a late-stage hurdle following employment tests and structured interviews|During the final induction and workplace orientation seminar|Option C|Reference checks are generally conducted later in the selection sequence, often after interviews and tests, to verify background information for serious contenders.
8.1|How does recruitment differ conceptually from selection within personnel management?|Recruitment is about narrowing down candidates while selection is about attracting them|Recruitment focuses on generating a broad applicant pool whereas selection involves choosing the best fit|Recruitment is an internal procedure while selection is strictly an external process|Recruitment involves medical and placement checks while selection involves onboarding|Option B|Recruitment widens the prospective talent pool by attracting applicants, whereas selection acts as a hurdle system to filter and choose the best candidate.
8.1|Why are medical and physical examinations placed near the end of the traditional selection hurdles sequence?|To ensure that medical screenings are only performed on serious finalists who have passed cognitive and interview hurdles|To determine the initial salary grade and promotion trajectory of the applicant before employment testing|To advertise physical job requirements to prospective candidates during the initial recruitment phase|To introduce the candidate to company medical staff during the induction process|Option A|Medical checks are costly and legally sensitive, so organizations typically reserve them for top finalists who have successfully cleared earlier evaluation hurdles.

9.1|When a worker decodes an incoming message from management, what is the primary cognitive action they are performing?|Converting thoughts into symbols for transmission|Selecting the appropriate medium to bypass interference|Interpreting and assigning meaning to the symbols received from the sender|Evaluating alternative policies against corporate objectives|Option C|Decoding is the process where the receiver interprets and extracts meaning from the symbols and signals sent by the encoder.
9.1|Which organizational communication direction is most vulnerable to distortion, speculation, and unverified rumors because it lacks official administrative oversight?|Downward communication|Upward communication|Horizontal communication|The grapevine|Option D|The grapevine operates informally without official checks and balances, making it highly susceptible to speculation, distortion, and rumor propagation.
9.1|What is the functional purpose of incorporating a feedback mechanism into the downward transmission of organizational instructions and policies?|To eliminate all potential sources of physical noise|To verify whether subordinates accurately understood the intended message|To convert formal policies into informal social networking chatter|To replace the need for horizontal peer coordination entirely|Option B|Feedback allows management to verify if the downward message was correctly received, interpreted, and understood by the subordinates.
11.1|Which performance appraisal technique involves a manager recording specific examples of exceptionally good or poor employee behavior throughout the evaluation period?|Graphic rating scale|Critical incidents method|Management by Objectives|360-degree feedback|Option B|The critical incidents method requires supervisors to document specific critical behaviors that illustrate outstanding or unsatisfactory performance to serve as concrete appraisal evidence.
11.1|What rating error occurs when a supervisor evaluates an employee based on one prominent positive trait, which unfairly influences the rating of all other unrelated performance dimensions?|Horns effect|Leniency bias|Halo effect|Recency effect|Option C|The halo effect happens when a single positive characteristic of an employee causes the rater to assign overly high scores across all other performance categories.
11.1|Which modern appraisal technique focuses on joint goal-setting and evaluating employees based on their progress toward mutually agreed-upon organizational objectives?|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales|Forced distribution method|Management by Objectives|Confidential reports|Option C|Management by Objectives (MBO) is a modern goal-driven approach where supervisors and subordinates collaborate to establish, monitor, and evaluate specific performance goals.
11.1|What systematic rating bias is present when a manager consistently avoids giving extreme scores, clustering all employee evaluations around the middle of the scale?|Central tendency bias|Strictness bias|Recency effect|Horns effect|Option A|Central tendency bias occurs when raters default to average or middle ratings for all employees, avoiding both exceptionally high and low marks regardless of actual performance.
11.1|Which appraisal method combines elements of the critical incidents technique with quantitative rating scales by anchoring specific behavioral descriptions to numerical performance levels?|Graphic rating scale|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales|Simple ranking method|360-degree feedback|Option B|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS) integrate graphic rating scales with specific behavioral anchors to provide clearer, more observable performance criteria.
11.1|What type of appraisal error occurs when an evaluator heavily weights an employee's performance from the last few weeks of the evaluation cycle while ignoring performance during the rest of the year?|Leniency bias|Central tendency bias|Recency effect|Halo effect|Option C|The recency effect causes raters to disproportionately focus on the most recent events or behaviors right before the appraisal review, neglecting the earlier parts of the evaluation period.
11.1|Which traditional appraisal technique requires an evaluator to list subordinates in order from the highest performer to the lowest performer?|Critical incidents|Graphic rating scales|Paired comparison|Ranking method|Option D|The ranking method is a traditional comparative technique where supervisors arrange their employees sequentially from best to worst overall performer.
11.1|What rating error takes place when a supervisor consistently rates all subordinates as below average or poor, holding an unrealistically high standard of evaluation?|Strictness bias|Leniency bias|Halo effect|Central tendency bias|Option A|Strictness bias happens when a rater is overly harsh and critical, systematically assigning lower scores than what employees actually deserve.
11.1|Which comprehensive appraisal technique gathers feedback from multiple rating sources including supervisors, peers, subordinates, and customers to provide a well-rounded performance review?|Management by Objectives|360-degree feedback|Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales|Forced distribution|Option B|360-degree feedback is a modern multi-source assessment method that collects performance insights from various stakeholders who interact with the employee.
11.1|What appraisal error occurs when a supervisor is consistently overly generous, rating nearly all subordinates near the top of the evaluation scale?|Strictness bias|Central tendency bias|Leniency bias|Recency effect|Option C|Leniency bias occurs when a rater avoids conflict or discomfort by granting inflated, overly favorable ratings to nearly all employees regardless of their actual output.
10.1|How does training fundamentally differ from development in human resource management?|Training focuses on short-term immediate technical skills while development targets long-term managerial growth|Training is broad theoretical knowledge whereas development is strictly physical labor|Training is meant for executives while development is designed exclusively for entry-level workers|Training deals with long-term career planning while development involves immediate task correction|Option A|Training is short-term and job-specific for immediate skills, whereas development is a long-term process aimed at overall personal and managerial growth.

10.1|During a Training Needs Assessment, what does a task analysis primarily seek to identify?|The specific skills duties and knowledge required to perform a job successfully|The overall profitability and financial health of the business enterprise|The personal psychological stability and emotional intelligence of individual workers|The historical background and founding principles of the organization|Option A|Task analysis breaks down the job requirements, standards, and duties to determine what specific knowledge and skills employees need to learn.
10.1|What is the core focus of a person analysis in the context of TNA?|Determining which specific employees require training and what their performance gaps are|Assessing the market demand for the company products and services|Evaluating the macroeconomic indicators affecting industry standards|Reviewing the physical layout and safety compliance of the workplace facilities|Option A|Person analysis evaluates individual employee performance against expected standards to identify who specifically needs training and in what areas.
10.1|Which of the following training methods is classified as an on-the-job training technique?|Job rotation|Lectures|Simulations|Vestibule training|Option A|Job rotation involves moving employees across different jobs or tasks within the actual workplace, making it a classic on-the-job training method.
10.1|What distinguishes education from training and development according to personnel management principles?|Education provides broad theoretical knowledge rather than immediate technical job skills|Education focuses exclusively on manual labor and machine operation|Education is always conducted inside a manufacturing factory setting|Education is a short-term intervention meant to fix immediate performance errors|Option A|Education emphasizes theoretical understanding, conceptual knowledge, and general intellectual growth rather than immediate technical task execution.
10.1|Which off-the-job training method allows learners to practice skills using replica equipment away from the actual pressure of the production floor?|Vestibule training|Apprenticeship|Coaching|Job rotation|Option A|Vestibule training utilizes simulated workspaces and duplicate equipment separate from the actual job site to train workers safely and effectively.
10.1|In which training approach does a seasoned employee or mentor directly guide a learner through daily work tasks over an extended period?|Coaching|Lectures|Role playing|Simulations|Option A|Coaching involves close, one-on-one guidance from an experienced mentor who provides continuous feedback and support on the job.
10.1|What is the primary objective of using role playing as an off-the-job training method?|To develop interpersonal skills and behavioral flexibility through simulated social scenarios|To teach complex mechanical engineering principles using textbooks|To assess the physical endurance and stamina of factory workers|To audit financial records and accounting compliance procedures|Option A|Role playing immerses participants in simulated interpersonal situations to help them practice communication, conflict resolution, and empathy.
10.1|Why is a comprehensive Training Needs Assessment considered a critical prerequisite before designing any training program?|It ensures that training resources are allocated efficiently to address actual performance gaps rather than guessed symptoms|It guarantees that every employee receives a promotion upon completion of the course|It eliminates the need for any further employee evaluations or performance appraisals|It legally obligates the government to subsidize corporate training expenses|Option A|TNA ensures that training interventions are targeted, cost-effective, and directly address verified deficiencies in organizational, task, or individual performance.
12.1|What is the fundamental focus of job evaluation in personnel management?|The individual performance and efficiency of the employee holding the position|The relative worth and value of the job itself rather than the person performing it|The market demand for specific job holders based on their educational background|The negotiation strategies used by trade unions during collective bargaining|Option B|Job evaluation systematically determines the relative worth of the job itself independent of individual employee performance.
12.1|Which of the following belongs to the category of non-quantitative job evaluation methods?|Point-factor method and factor comparison method|Market survey analysis and cost of living adjustment|Job ranking method and job classification grading method|Union bargaining agreements and minimum wage legislation|Option C|Ranking and classification or grading are traditional non-quantitative methods that evaluate whole jobs without assigning numerical points.
12.1|How does a quantitative job evaluation method differ fundamentally from a non-quantitative method?|It evaluates jobs based on holistic impressions rather than numerical metrics|It focuses exclusively on individual employee merit increases and bonuses|It uses numerical values and specific compensable factors to measure job worth|It relies entirely on external market surveys rather than internal job analysis|Option C|Quantitative methods break jobs down into compensable factors and assign numerical values to determine relative worth.
12.1|In the context of pay determinants, what does a market survey primarily help an organization establish?|Internal equity by comparing the worth of different departments within the firm|External competitiveness by reflecting what other employers are paying for similar jobs|The legal minimum wage mandated by federal or state labor laws|The precise cost of living adjustments required for individual employee retention|Option B|Market surveys provide vital data on external pay rates to ensure the organization remains competitive in attracting talent.
12.1|Which factor represents an external legal constraint on an organization's pay structure determination?|Internal job worth established through systematic job evaluation|Ability to pay determined by the company profitability and financial health|Minimum wage law set by governmental legislative bodies|Union bargaining power during collective agreement negotiations|Option C|Minimum wage laws are statutory, external legal regulations that establish the absolute lowest compensation an employer can legally pay.
12.1|What is the primary characteristic of the job classification or grading method?|Jobs are compared against a predetermined scale of job classes or grades with defined criteria|Jobs are ranked from highest to lowest in a single unbroken linear hierarchy|Jobs are broken down into precise mathematical points using compensable factors|Jobs are priced strictly according to regional cost of living indices and inflation rates|Option A|The classification method groups jobs into predefined grades or classes by comparing job descriptions to established standards.
12.1|When an organization adjusts its pay structure to compensate for rising inflation and consumer prices, which pay determinant is primarily being addressed?|Internal job worth via job evaluation results|Cost of living changes in the broader economy|Ability to pay based on annual corporate revenue|Market survey data from competing industries|Option B|Cost of living adjustments reflect changes in consumer prices and inflation to maintain the purchasing power of employee wages.
12.1|Which pay determinant directly reflects an organization's financial capacity and profitability?|Union bargaining demands during contract renewal periods|Ability to pay based on corporate revenue and financial health|Minimum wage law compliance mandated by state regulators|Market survey benchmarks gathered from local competitors|Option B|An organization's ability to pay is tied directly to its financial health, profitability, and overall budgetary capacity.
12.1|What is the main limitation of using the simple job ranking method in large organizations?|It requires complex mathematical formulas and computer software to calculate scores|It becomes cumbersome and subjective when dealing with a large number of diverse jobs|It relies too heavily on external market surveys instead of internal job analysis|It requires strict adherence to statutory minimum wage laws and union contracts|Option B|Ranking whole jobs becomes unwieldy, subjective, and difficult to manage as the number of unique positions in an organization increases.
12.1|How do union bargaining agreements influence the compensation management process?|They dictate the absolute internal job evaluation points for management positions|They establish legally binding pay rates and structures through collective negotiations|They replace the need for market surveys and cost of living adjustments completely|They determine the individual merit performance ratings of non-union employees|Option B|Union bargaining involves collective negotiations that result in binding agreements determining pay scales and salary increases.
13.1|According to the Trade Unions Act framework within the Nigerian context, what is the fundamental legal definition of a trade union?|A permanent political party established to contest legislative seats on behalf of labor|A temporary coalition of employers designed to fix market prices for commodities|A combination of workers or employers whether temporary or permanent formed to regulate terms and conditions of employment|An informal social club organized strictly for employee welfare and recreational outings|Option C|A trade union is legally defined as a combination of workers or employers formed primarily to regulate employer-employee relations and terms of employment.
13.1|Which of the following represents a primary economic and protective objective of trade unions as outlined in labor management principles?|Securing higher wages and enhanced job security for union members|Minimizing corporate tax liabilities for multinational business enterprises|Directly managing corporate share distribution on the stock exchange|Abolishing all forms of labor legislation to promote total deregulation|Option A|Trade unions primarily exist to protect workers' interests by negotiating higher wages and establishing strong job security measures.
13.1|What distinguishes an industrial union structure from other forms of labor organization within the Nigerian labor landscape?|It organizes workers based strictly on their geographical residential districts rather than workplaces|It encompasses all workers regardless of skill within a specific industry such as petroleum or education|It represents exclusively executive-level management personnel across various diverse sectors|It operates solely as a temporary ad-hoc committee during national elections|Option B|Industrial unions organize all workers within a specific industry regardless of their particular craft or trade classification.
13.1|Which of the following organizations is a prominent example of an industrial union operating in Nigeria?|Nigeria Labour Congress|Trade Union Congress|Academic Staff Union of Universities|Manufacturers Association of Nigeria|Option C|ASUU is a classic example of an industrial and professional union operating within the Nigerian tertiary education sector.
13.1|What is the structural designation of the Academic Staff Union of Universities within the Nigerian labor framework?|Central labor organization representing all Nigerian workers|General labor federation for informal sector artisans|Industrial union representing academic staff in public universities|Employers association representing university governing councils|Option C|ASUU functions as an industrial union specifically structured to represent university academic personnel.
13.1|Which of the following labor entities functions as a central labor body in Nigeria rather than an individual industrial union?|Nigeria Labour Congress|Academic Staff Union of Universities|Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers|Nigeria Union of Teachers|Option A|The Nigeria Labour Congress acts as a central umbrella labor body coordinating various industrial unions nationwide.
13.1|What primary structural role does the Trade Union Congress play within the Nigerian industrial relations system?|Serving as a central labor body representing senior staff associations|Acting as a single employer trade group for private manufacturing firms|Regulating international trade tariffs for imported industrial machinery|Enforcing labor tax compliance across state government ministries|Option A|The Trade Union Congress operates as a central labor body primarily coordinating senior staff associations in Nigeria.
13.1|What is the primary legal purpose of a statutory cooling-off period prior to the execution of an industrial strike action?|To allow employers to permanently dismiss union leaders without legal recourse|To provide a mandatory window for conciliation and dispute resolution before work stoppage|To enable the government to dissolve all registered trade unions indefinitely|To force workers to sign individual employment contracts renouncing union membership|Option B|A statutory cooling-off period provides a mandatory legal window for dialogue and mediation to resolve disputes before a strike.
13.1|Which of the following Nigerian unions is specifically classified as an industrial union within the petroleum sector?|Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers|Nigeria Labour Congress|Trade Union Congress|Nigeria Union of Teachers|Option A|NUPENG is an established industrial union representing workers within the Nigerian petroleum and natural gas sector.
13.1|Which organizational objective is considered a core operational goal for trade unions concerning workplace standards?|Securing better working conditions and maintaining occupational safety standards|Maximizing annual dividend payouts for corporate shareholders|Eliminating labor productivity metrics across all manufacturing plants|Restricting employee training programs to lower operational costs|Option A|Securing better working conditions and safety standards is a core objective of trade unionism to protect worker welfare.
14.1|Which of the following best defines a grievance in the context of personnel management as outlined in the study notes?|A formal complaint raised by an employee regarding issues such as contract interpretation wages promotion or workplace safety|An informal verbal discussion between colleagues regarding daily operational workloads and personal preferences|A unilateral directive issued by executive management to restructure the organizational hierarchy and reduce overhead costs|A collective bargaining agreement negotiated between labor unions and employers prior to the formal hiring process|Option A|A grievance is specifically defined as a formal complaint over contract interpretation wages promotion or safety matters within the workplace.
14.1|What is the first step in the statutory settlement machinery for resolving industrial grievances and disputes in Nigeria?|Referring the dispute directly to the National Industrial Court of Nigeria|Initiating the internal grievance procedure within the organization|Appointing an independent conciliator through the Federal Minister of Labour|Submitting a formal brief to the Industrial Arbitration Panel for an official award|Option B|The statutory framework mandates that dispute resolution must begin at the foundational level through the internal grievance procedure.
14.1|Within the statutory machinery framework what is the designated time frame for mediation as a voluntary third-party intervention?|Within 7 days of the dispute arising or escalating|Within 14 days following the initial conciliation hearing|Within 30 days prior to the Industrial Arbitration Panel review|Within 48 hours of filing an appeal at the National Industrial Court|Option A|Mediation functions as a voluntary third-party intervention that is structured to take place within 7 days.
14.1|Who holds the statutory authority to appoint a conciliator during the third stage of the grievance settlement machinery in Nigeria?|The President of the National Industrial Court|The Director of the Industrial Arbitration Panel|The Minister of Labour|The Head of the Internal Grievance Committee|Option C|The Minister of Labour is vested with the statutory power to appoint a conciliator to assist parties in reaching a voluntary settlement.
14.1|What is the formal output generated by the Industrial Arbitration Panel when handling an industrial dispute?|An administrative memorandum|An arbitral award|A judicial injunction|A mediation transcript|Option B|The Industrial Arbitration Panel resolves disputes referred to it by issuing an official arbitral award.
14.1|Which body possesses exclusive jurisdiction over trade disputes and industrial relations matters at the apex of the Nigerian statutory machinery?|The National Industrial Court of Nigeria|The Supreme Court of Nigeria|The Federal High Court|The Industrial Arbitration Panel Appeals Board|Option A|The National Industrial Court of Nigeria holds exclusive judicial jurisdiction for final adjudication of trade disputes.
14.1|If an internal grievance procedure fails to resolve a dispute between management and an employee what is the immediate subsequent statutory step?|Conciliation by an independent ministerially appointed agent|Mediation utilizing a voluntary third party|Arbitration leading to a binding panel award|Adjudication through the National Industrial Court|Option B|Following internal procedures the machinery proceeds to voluntary third-party mediation within 7 days before advancing to conciliation.
14.1|Which of the following issues would properly constitute the basis of a formal workplace grievance under personnel management principles?|Disagreements over the interpretation of an employment contract and wage structures|General dissatisfaction with national economic inflation rates and fiscal policies|Personal personality conflicts occurring completely outside the scope of employment duties|Corporate branding strategies and long-term marketing portfolio expansion plans|Option A|Contract interpretation and wage disputes directly affect the terms of employment and form the core basis of a formal grievance.
14.1|What role does conciliation play in the statutory machinery compared to mediation?|Conciliation is handled exclusively by an official appointed by the Minister of Labour whereas mediation is a voluntary third-party step within 7 days|Conciliation represents the final appellate court whereas mediation is an internal corporate review process|Conciliation issues binding judicial orders while mediation only gathers witness testimonies|Conciliation replaces the internal grievance procedure entirely for public sector employees|Option A|Conciliation involves an official appointed by the Minister of Labour as a distinct statutory stage succeeding the 7-day voluntary mediation window.
14.1|Why is the internal grievance procedure placed as the mandatory first step in statutory settlement machinery?|To ensure issues are addressed closest to the source before escalating to external regulatory bodies|To allow the National Industrial Court to bypass preliminary hearings and save judicial time|To permit external labor unions to bypass management and negotiate directly with the government|To eliminate the need for written documentation during the early stages of a dispute|Option A|Starting internally allows organizations to resolve complaints at the lowest possible level and closest to the source before involving external machinery.
15.1|According to John Dunlop's Systems Model of industrial relations, what are the primary structural components that interact within the system?|Management, trade unions, and the state|Shareholders, board of directors, and consumers|Human resources department, payroll staff, and employees|Suppliers, regulatory bodies, and competitors|Option A|Dunlop's framework identifies the three central actors in an industrial relations system as employers/management, employees/unions, and the state/government.
15.1|In the context of industrial relations, which of the following best describes the primary function of the state or government within Dunlop's model?|Acting as an environmental regulator and establishing the legal framework for labor interactions|Directly setting executive compensation packages for private corporations|Internal dispute arbitration exclusively for non-unionized establishments|Managing daily human resource operations for manufacturing firms|Option A|The state acts as a regulatory authority and framework-setter that influences and shapes the interactions between employers and employee representatives.
15.1|What is the defining characteristic of collective bargaining as outlined in industrial relations study sessions?|A bilateral negotiation process between management and union leaders resulting in legally binding agreements|A unilateral policy implementation by management regarding workplace safety protocols|An informal mediation session facilitated by third-party psychologists to improve morale|A government-imposed wage freeze applied across all industrial sectors|Option A|Collective bargaining is formally defined as negotiations between management and union representatives specifically designed to establish legally binding terms on wages, hours, and conditions.
15.1|Which of the following outcomes is a direct and typical product of successful collective bargaining between a union and management?|A formalized and legally enforceable collective agreement governing employment terms|An indefinite strike action by employees with no legal termination date|A corporate merger document defining market share expansion strategies|A unilateral managerial memo outlining unchangeable workplace rules|Option A|The culmination of collective bargaining is a legally binding contract or agreement that governs wages, hours, and working conditions for the bargaining unit.
15.1|When analyzing John Dunlop's industrial relations model, how do the three core actors primarily function?|They interact within a shared environmental context shaped by market constraints, technology, and power distributions|They operate entirely independently without any mutual influence or shared constraints|They compete exclusively in product markets to maximize shareholder equity returns|They function as a single hierarchical corporate structure with centralized authority|Option A|Dunlop conceptualized industrial relations as a social system where management, unions, and government interact continuously under specific environmental contexts.
15.1|Which specific subjects are traditionally mandated as core agenda items during collective bargaining negotiations?|Wages, working hours, and general terms and conditions of employment|Corporate tax optimization strategies and international supply chain logistics|Consumer pricing models and quarterly marketing budget allocations|Internal corporate board member election procedures and shareholder dividends|Option A|Core collective bargaining issues fundamentally center on the economic and operational relationship between employer and workers, specifically wages, hours, and employment terms.
15.1|Within Dunlop's Systems Model, what role do trade unions play as one of the principal actors?|Representing collective employee interests and negotiating standardized labor standards with management|Providing direct venture capital funding for corporate expansions and acquisitions|Enforcing criminal statutes within industrial manufacturing facilities|Designing enterprise resource planning software for administrative staff|Option A|Trade unions act as the organized voice of employees, engaging directly with employers to protect worker interests and negotiate employment terms.
15.1|Why is the output of collective bargaining considered legally binding rather than merely advisory?|Because it creates enforceable contractual obligations that both management and union members must legally uphold|Because it is enforced by international criminal tribunals rather than civil courts|Because it relies entirely on voluntary compliance without any legal recourse for breach|Because it represents a moral guideline rather than a formal employment contract|Option A|Collective bargaining agreements carry legal weight, meaning both parties are bound by law to adhere to the agreed-upon provisions regarding wages, hours, and conditions.
15.1|In the study of industrial relations, which actor is primarily responsible for directing production and utilizing labor within the enterprise?|Employers and management|Elected trade union shop stewards|Ministry of labor inspectors and industrial court judges|Consolidated consumer advocacy coalitions|Option A|Management represents the employer side of the industrial relations triad, holding the primary responsibility for organizing production and directing enterprise operations.
15.1|How does Dunlop's model view the relationship between the three industrial relations actors and their surrounding environment?|The actors interact within an environment defined by technology, market constraints, and the distribution of power in society|The actors exist in a vacuum completely detached from economic conditions or technological changes|The environment dictates every single action with zero influence or agency from the actors themselves|The actors create an artificial environment that has no relation to the broader political economy|Option A|Dunlop emphasized that the actors do not operate in isolation; their interactions are deeply shaped and constrained by the external economic, technological, and power environment.
1.1|Which historical phase of personnel management primarily emerged as a direct response to the operational pressures and workforce demands of the World Wars?|Welfare Officer Phase|Labour Manager Phase|Personnel Management Phase|Strategic Human Resource Management Phase|Option B|The Labour Manager phase evolved during World War I and II when rapid industrial production required specialized management of labor supply, recruitment, and shop-floor conflicts.
1.1|In the chronological evolution of personnel management, which phase is characterized by a shift toward treating employees as strategic assets aligned with long-term organizational goals?|Welfare Officer Phase|Labour Manager Phase|Personnel Management Phase|Strategic Human Resource Management|Option D|Strategic Human Resource Management views human resources as a vital source of competitive advantage, integrating people management directly into corporate strategy.
1.1|The institutional roots of personnel management in Nigeria can be traced back to the administrative machinery of the colonial civil service and the operational footprint of which major commercial trading corporation?|United Africa Company|John Holt Plc|Standard Bank Nigeria|PZ Cussons Nigeria|Option A|The United Africa Company played a foundational role in shaping early corporate labor relations and employment practices within the Nigerian private sector context.
1.1|Which foundational Nigerian public commission report notably recommended comprehensive administrative reforms and professionalization across the public service, shifting it towards a results-oriented approach?|Morgan Commission of 1963|Adebo Commission of 1970|Udoji Public Service Review Commission of 1974|Gorsuch Commission of 1954|Option C|The Udoji Commission of 1974 famously advocated for a results-oriented public service, emphasizing management by objectives and modern personnel management techniques.
1.1|What was the specific legislative instrument that originally established the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria (CIPMN) in 1992?|Decree No. 58 of 1992|Decree No. 14 of 1988|Act No. 22 of 1995|Decree No. 43 of 1993|Option A|CIPMN was originally established by Decree 58 of 1992, which later transitioned into an Act of the National Assembly, giving statutory backing to human resource practice in Nigeria.
1.1|During which historical period did the Welfare Officer Phase predominantly emerge, focusing heavily on working conditions, housing, and basic employee welfare?|Post-World War II era|Late 19th Century Industrial period|The Great Depression era|The 1970 oil boom period|Option B|The Welfare Officer Phase emerged in the late 19th century as early industrialists appointed welfare secretaries to mitigate harsh factory conditions and look after worker wellbeing.
1.1|Which of the following commissions primarily focused on wage reviews and cost-of-living adjustments in Nigeria prior to the landmark structural reforms of the 1970s?|Udoji Commission|Morgan Commission of 1963|Phillipson-Adebo Commission|Dotun Phillips Panel|Option B|The Morgan Commission of 1963 was established primarily to review wages, salaries, and working conditions across Nigeria in response to intense labor agitations.
1.1|What primary transformation distinguished the Personnel Management Phase from its preceding Labour Manager Phase in the post-war era?|An exclusive focus on legal compliance and union suppression|A broader scope encompassing psychological testing training and structured industrial relations|The complete abandonment of welfare programs in favor of automation|A shift toward decentralized management handled entirely by line supervisors without specialists|Option C|The post-war Personnel Management phase expanded beyond basic labor coordination to incorporate systematic personnel functions like training, welfare, and formal industrial relations.
1.1|Which entity holds the legal mandate for regulating and setting professional standards for human resource practice in Nigeria today?|Nigeria Employers Consultative Association|Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment|Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria|Nigerian Institute of Management|Option C|CIPMN, established under Nigerian law, is the sole statutory body empowered to regulate, train, and certify personnel management professionals in the country.
1.1|How did the Adebo Commission of 1970 significantly influence Nigerian labor dynamics?|By introducing performance-related budgeting across all federal ministries|By addressing major wage demands and recommending interim awards alongside structural review of salaries|By legally establishing the trade union congress as the sole umbrella body|By decentralizing civil service recruitment to regional authorities|Option B|The Adebo Commission was set up to review wages and salaries, addressing cost-of-living pressures and making key recommendations on compensation structures in Nigeria.
